ai_summary.headline: Somalia has made MPCA the first-line modality on paper, but only about a third of the USD 97M is funded.
ai_summary.narrative: Cash is unusually prominent in the 2026 plan. MPC is a dedicated USD 97M line (11.4% of the USD 852M appeal) and, per the gDCF reading of the HNRP, total CVA is USD 365.5M, 43% of requirements [s1][s5]. The Humanitarian Coordinator calls MPCA the first-line response modality and the CWG issued a framework in February 2026 making it the default for households with multiple needs [s2][s11]. Funding does not yet match the ambition: the plan is 35.5% funded and MPC has received USD 35.1M, 36.2% of its line [s1]. The pooled fund shows no MPC-tagged projects in 2025 or 2026, so MPC relies on bilateral donors [s6]. Household preference looks split rather than cash-dominant: 78% named cash and 78% in-kind in the 2025 MSNA [s7]. Market monitoring appears to be in place through FSNAU/FEWS NET [s12]. The CWG is co-led by WFP and Concern with an OCHA co-chair role [s9][s14]; no cash feasibility study was found.
barriers: MPC funding is 36% of its line, so the first-line modality may not be deliverable at scale
Pooled fund allocations carry no MPC cluster tag
Cash and in-kind are tied in stated preference, which supports mixed responses
Cluster sections of the HNRP are reported to vary in CVA depth [s5]
opportunities: HC-level endorsement of MPCA gives CALP a clear advocacy hook for pooled-fund and bilateral funding
MPCA exit pathway to the Baxnaano safety net links humanitarian cash to national systems [s5]
data_gaps: sectoral cash share of funding and pooled funds
